name: Calle Jorge: flagged west entrance, tiled path and cross-paths, lawns and kerbs, planter walls, benches, beds, planting, plaques, sign and lamp
trust: IMG_2182, IMG_2229, IMG_2230 and IMG_2234 look along Calle Jorge: about four square terracotta tiles across (0.36 m each), joints running with the path and not on the diagonal, a pale concrete edge, then lawn. Lawn side: the lawn runs from the path to the house fronts (the aerial shows it from about 95 to 127 m). IMG_2182 and IMG_2229 show a two-tile cross-path with the same pale edge leaving the lane about 1.9 m east of the bench (read from the tile rows and the horizon in both photos), and IMG_2229 and IMG_2231 show a second path that leaves the lane about 4 m west of the bench, runs diagonally behind it and on along the house front past a white-kerbed bed with three round clipped shrubs and a strelitzia, with a climber trained on the wall behind; a smaller kerbed shrub stands on the lawn west of the bench (the aerial shows its white kerb at about 106.5 m). Where the paths run between the lane and the houses is estimated to about 1 m. IMG_2231 and IMG_2232 are the bench, IMG_2596 the path beside it with a round red SANEA cover and a square grate; IMG_2231 also shows house number 20. The one photographed bench is the station at 112 m; no photo shows a second bench, and three more are placed from the aerial (see benches.aerialBasis). IMG_2234 shows the CALLE DE TEODORO plaque on the lawn-side wall with a bougainvillea over it, a tall clipped hedge on the lawn in front, yellow lantana behind the hedge, a green round cover in the grass, and slot drains and square grates across the path where the octagon-tiled lane of IMG_2235 joins from the hedge side. Hedge side, from west to east: a white planter wall with a clipped hedge standing at the path edge (IMG_2234); the octagon-tiled lane (the mapped Teodoro Rojo line at 93.4 m); then an open garden lawn edged by a white-painted kerb that turns back along that lane, with one black lamp post on the kerb corner (IMG_2234, IMG_2235) and a dragon tree on the lawn near the lane (IMG_2230, IMG_2182). IMG_2183 and IMG_2233 are taken across that lawn, which is open to the lane with no wall or hedge in front: the candelabra tree stands towards the back, a few pale trunks and a broad crown of curved, winged stems about twice the height of the garden wall behind it, over a bed of lantana, with a bougainvillea trained along that wall. Its 5.6 m height, 4.2 m spread and place on the lawn are estimates. East of the garden the planters resume in front of the patios (IMG_2182, IMG_2230): about 0.7 m high, a clipped hedge in each, broken by two brick-paved thresholds about 1.1 m wide with a short planter between them; a small recess with a blue-and-white number tile sits by each threshold (the digits are not legible, so none are modelled). Gap stations are read from the pins and are good to about 2 m. Only one lamp post is seen along the lane (the kerb corner); IMG_2234 shows wall lanterns, not posts, further west, so the posts formerly at 88, 92 and 118 m were removed. IMG_2597 is the CALLE DE JORGE plinth and black lamp at the east end, standing on a lawn with an old olive beside it; the plinth's lettered face is turned towards the path and the camera (south-west), not along the lane. Lawn, wall and planting are not continued between the west entrance (see west, to about 28 m) and the photographed east stretch. Pins are ±2 to ±5 m and no camera is solved, so every station here is an estimate.

benches.aerialBasis: Dave, 2026-11-11: there is more than one bench on Calle Jorge. The aerial (Esri World Imagery, zoom 19, public/map/ground.jpg, 0.24 m a pixel) shows white marks about 1.5 m long with a shadow, standing 1.6 to 1.9 m off the path on grass, at about 64.3 and 79.2 m on the north side and 122.3 m on the south side (docs/reviews/jorge-benches-aerial/). A fourth, similar mark at 106.5 m is read as the white-kerbed shrub bed that IMG_2229 and IMG_2230 show west of the bench, because those photos look along that lawn and show no second bench. Open: the aerial shows nothing at 112 m, where the pins put the photographed bench, so that bench may really be the 106.5 m mark, with the pins about 5 m too far east; no camera is solved to settle it. No photo shows the three aerial benches, so which way each faces and whether each is a bench at all is inferred; they are good to about 1 m along the lane.

west.basis: IMG_2280 and IMG_2696-2698 stand in the Pintor Dalí car park at the west end of the mapped Calle Jorge line and look east-north-east along it (headings 56 to 65 degrees; the line runs 60). They show a path of irregular sandstone flags about 2 m wide between two white-painted kerbs the length of the parking bays, the left kerb ending in a short return beside a black lamp post that carries a camera, then lawn on both sides with the flagged path running on to a white gateway. Two round clipped trees stand on the left (north) lawn; on the right a border of clipped and yellow-flowering shrubs runs along a house with a purple bougainvillea over its first floor. The aerial agrees: parked cars to about 7 m, a 9 m deep lawn with two tree crowns on the north side, a house 3.4 m off on the south side, and a white mark on the line at about 28 m read as the gateway. The flags are built to 28 m; the gateway itself, and whether flags or terracotta lie beyond it, are not known. Kerb length, path width and plant positions are estimated to about 1 m; no camera is solved.

guillermoPlanter.basis: IMG_2773 looks up Calle Guillermo from the Jorge junction and IMG_2774 from 9 m further on: a neat, straight white planter wall about a metre high (waist height beside the lane), about 0.45 m thick, with a low dense carpet of orange and yellow lantana along its top, runs along the lane's east side to the steps of the pool building. A clump of spiky yucca or dragon-tree heads rises from behind it about a third of the way along; there is no palm beside it. IMG_2597 shows the same wall behind the lawn of the CALLE DE JORGE plinth. The wall's top is set one metre above the lane surface beside it. It is built from 3 to 25 m north of the Jorge line; IMG_2822 and IMG_2823 show it also continues south past the junction and round towards the sea, which is not built.

guillermoPaving.basis: IMG_2773 and IMG_2774 look up Calle Guillermo from the Jorge junction: the lane is paved wall to wall, about 2.3 m wide between the plinth lawn and the planter, in large terracotta squares at the junction and then, from about 3 m north, in terracotta octagons with small square insets (five or six across), on towards the steps of the pool building. A round cast cover and two rectangular grates lie in the octagons. IMG_2822 and IMG_2823 show the same octagons south of the junction. In IMG_2773 the squares are about 1.4 times the octagon pitch, so they are drawn 0.56 m against 0.4 m octagons; the real sizes are not known. The paving is laid from 5 m south to 25 m north of the Jorge line (squares for the 6 m up to 3 m north) on the mapped Guillermo line, against the planter's lane face, which closes the grass strip the model had between wall and lane. Width and cover positions are estimated to about 0.5 m.

guillermoWest.basis: Dave, 2026-11-12: from the IMG_2773 viewpoint the houses on the left do not match the photo. IMG_2773 and IMG_2774 show, west of Calle Guillermo: the plinth lawn with a small broad-leaved tree and a rose bush; along the lawn's north side a plain white wall with no door or window, bougainvillea trained along it, its top falling from well over a storey high on the left to about 2.6 m at the lane (6.6 times the 0.4 m sign plate, and 2.8 m against the 3.8 m lamp post), where it ends in a pier carrying a no-dogs sign near its top; then, along the lane, low white planters with clipped hedges, broken by gateways, with a taller white patio wall behind them, strelitzia leaves showing above it and two lamp posts; a row of bricks on edge borders the lane. The houses stand back behind these walls, with chimneys showing. The wall along the lawn lies on the registry edge of part 6364401UF1366S_part7 (11.2 m north of the Jorge line), so that face and its return are kept clear of the generic doors, shutters and porches, and the wall is continued 3 m east to the lane with a falling top. The planters, patio wall and lamp posts stand on ground the registry leaves empty, where the aerial shows walled patios. Open: plants show above the lawn wall in the photo, so the east part of part7 is probably an open patio and not a roofed room; the registry block is left as it is (a footprint change needs a measured check), which makes the wall top level where the photo's falls. Planter, gateway and lamp positions are read from the two photos and good to about 1.5 m; the patio wall's position is good to about 1 m.

lawnPalm.basis: IMG_2764 and IMG_2765 look across the main-pool lawn from below Calle Jorge: tall slender palms, the trunk three to four times the height of a compact crown, stand on the lawn towards the pool, the nearest about 19 m from the camera on a bearing of about 330 degrees (it is left of centre in IMG_2764 and just right of centre in IMG_2765; the distance is read from where its foot meets the lawn). It replaces two short, thick generic palms: one that stood against the Guillermo planter (object enrique-steps-4), where IMG_2773 shows a yucca clump and no palm, and one 5 m in front of this camera (main-pool-2), where IMG_2764, IMG_2765 and IMG_2598 show open lawn. Position is good to about 4 m; the 15 m height follows from that distance.

photographed.basis: Every Calle Jorge photo was taken between 101 and 130 m along the mapped centreline (IMG_2182-2234, IMG_2596, IMG_2597); IMG_2234 looks about 15 m further west. West of about 86 m nothing is photographed, so the lane keeps the generic ribbon there (gap:jorge-west, photo request jorge-west-walk), except the west entrance from the Dalí car park, which has its own photos (see west).
